newsitem.title: USA: Grigsby resignation won't affect Miami arena deal.
newsitem.headline: Grigsby resignation won't affect Miami arena deal.

text.p: Grigsby Branford & Co Inc is still on tap to act as senior manager for Dade County's $165 million basketball arena bond issue, despite the resignation of the firm's president, county finance manager Ed Marquez said Friday.
"The loss of Cal Grigsby to the firm itself should not damage the firm's ability to effectively do bond transactions," Marquez said. "The firm is still intact."
Grigsby, who was recently fined $5,000 for laundering a campaign contribution in California, resigned from the firm last week.
Grigsby Brandford is among 20 firms in Dade County's standing pool of bond underwriters and has acted as co-manager or senior manager for nine Dade issues in the last four years.
Most recently, the firm was senior manager for last month's $183 million Dade County revenue bond refinancing for the Montenay Power Corp recyling plant.

The Miami Herald printed allegations Friday that former city manager Howard Gary won his firm a spot in the syndicate for that deal by offering Dade County Commissioner James Burke $100,000. The newspaper said Gary was cooperating with federal prosecutors and wore a hidden wire to tape record conversations implacating Burke.

Burke, who unavailable for comment Friday, told the newspaper he played no role in getting Grigsby selected as senior manager for the deal. Marquez and other said the underwriters were selected by the recycling company.
Asked if there was any reason to consider removing Grigsby from the county's bond pool, Marquez said no, then added, "It also depends on what comes out."

The arena bond deal may never materialize for unrelated reasons. Bond proceeds are to finance construction of a new arena for the Miami Heat on public park land adjacent to the Port of Miami. Opponents obtained enough voter signatures to force a Nov 5 referendum on the financing proposal, and several polls have incidated the measure could fail.

In a move that infuriated opponents to the arena deal, the Dade County Commission reworded the ballot language last week so that those who oppose the deal must vote 'yes' and those who support it must vote 'no.'
